newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR EXTENDS LOSSES ON HARD UNITS.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR EXTENDS LOSSES ON HARD UNITS.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar lost further ground against hard currencies on Wednesday, with rumours flying around the interbank market of a big import payment coming up, dealers said.
"We've seen a lot of buying in the market since late yesterday...the Reserve Bank hasn't come in (with support)," one dealer said.

"There's rumour of a big payment coming through but I'm not sure how true it is. But when things start happening like this and the Reserve Bank doesn't come in people usually start panicking, buying a lot and holding onto cash," he said, adding:
"There could be a payment but the larger part of it is all speculation, I think."

At around 0740 GMT, the Zimbabwe dollar was trading at 11.2500/2600 versus the U.S. currency, a cent down from 11.2400/2500 at the close of business on Tuesday and slipped to 17.9075/9350 from 17.8300/8500 against pound sterling.
It was at 6.6945/7045 on the mark from 6.6700/6900 and was also quoted a touch weaker against the rand at 2.5410/5460 compared to 2.5400/5600.
